name: Shallum
overview: Shallum was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified specifically as the son of Sismai. His lineage is briefly noted in the genealogical records without additional biographical details. There are no further notes expanding on his life or role beyond his tribal affiliation and paternal connection.
namesAndTitles: The name Shallum means 'peace, well-being, prosperity' in Hebrew, reflecting a positive and hopeful meaning. It is a proper name mentioned in Scripture but was not given directly by God. This name appears in the genealogical context of 1 Chronicles 2:40.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Shallum as the son of Sismai and the father of Jekamiah. These family ties are explicitly stated in 1 Chronicles 2:40-41, establishing his place within the Judahite lineage. No other family relationships are documented beyond these connections.
scriptureSignificance: Shallum's significance lies primarily in his role within the genealogical framework of the tribe of Judah. As the son of Sismai and father of Jekamiah, he represents a link in the ancestral line that preserves the heritage of God's chosen people. Though not highlighted for specific deeds or leadership, Shallum's mention affirms the continuity of God's promises through the generations of Judah.
